stories.headline: Tesla files $10.1B 'Project Crystal Sun' solar-cell factory tax-incentive application in Fort Bend County, TX (filed Aug 11); ingot-to-module facility, ~9,712 permanent jobs, construction 2026-2028, commercial production targeted Q1 2029; company says it is still evaluating a competing out-of-state site so the commitment is non-binding; VC Chamath Palihapitiya's Aug 12 'all in on nuclear/solar' post amplified retail attention

Tesla China July wholesale sales: 93,579 units, highest month of 2026, +37.85% YoY, 9th straight month of YoY growth — counters the soft-EV-demand/BYD-share-loss narrative for the Shanghai plant (>50% of global output)

National Highway Traffic Safety Administration closes investigation into 695,000 Model 3/Y vehicles; Tesla safety updates resolved concerns
NHTSA escalates FSD camera-only probe to formal Engineering Analysis; 24-part information demand due Aug 12; outcome by mid-August determines formal recall trigger
Tesla launches Robotaxi in Orlando & Tampa on Jul 21, expanding Florida footprint to 3 metros in <3 weeks (Miami Jul 3, Orlando/Tampa Jul 21); full unsupervised rides from day one
Tesla launches Model Y L (longer wheelbase) Launch Series for U.S. orders; $61,990 entry price, 6-seat config, includes 12-month free FSD subscription, Oct-Nov delivery window
Tesla recalls 14,575 units (2025-2026 Model Y) for missing federal certification label; automation tool failure during production; notices by Jul 17
Tesla recalls 2017, 2021-2023 Model 3/Y/S/X for delayed rearview camera image when vehicle placed in reverse; notices mailed Jul 3, 2026
Insider executive buy: $650,000 purchase on Jul 20, timed right before Q2 earnings announcement; contrasts with routine pre-scheduled 10b5-1 selling pattern
Wisconsin carrier Paper Transport announces formal Chicago metro pilot partnership with Tesla Semi Long Range; signals commercial operator confidence in production readiness
Europe registered 118,068 Tesla vehicles (first 5 months 2026), up 57.2% YoY; validates geographic diversification and pricing power
Piper Sandler cuts Tesla price target from $500 to $450 on Jul 28; continues post-Q2 earnings analyst downgrade cycle
Tesla builds its 10-millionth vehicle (Jul 30, Fremont); marks halfway progress toward the 20M-vehicle goal in one of the four operational tranches of Musk's $1T pay package

Tesla-SpaceX merger speculation intensifies: Kalshi prediction-market odds hit a record 74% for a merger by May 2027, following Musk's Jul 22 earnings-call comment about 'growing overlap' (Terafab); no formal process confirmed by either company

WSJ reports Tesla executives were told to explore separating/selling the China business ahead of a possible Tesla-SpaceX merger (SpaceX's defense-contractor status seen as incompatible with Tesla's China manufacturing footprint); Musk denies on X: 'This has never even come up in a discussion ever. Absurdly fake news.'

DOT/NHTSA announces AV-deregulation package: Zoox-specific temporary robotaxi exemption (2,500/yr) and a fast-tracked national AV performance standard to replace the current state patchwork; not Tesla-specific but a directional tailwind for robotaxi deployment broadly

NHTSA opens preliminary evaluation into ~1.2M Tesla vehicles (2018-2020 Model 3, 2021-2023 Model Y) over front lower lateral-link suspension detachment; 156 owner complaints, no confirmed crashes/injuries; could escalate to a recall

Tesla and SpaceX confirm Grimes County, TX as the site for their joint 'Terafab' chip plant: $16.8B first-phase investment, 100M+ sq ft planned footprint, 3,000+ jobs; chips earmarked for Optimus, Cybercab, and SpaceX space-based data centers

Reuters investigation: Tesla pressured Dutch regulator RDW since late 2024 to keep FSD safety-review documentation sealed, citing 'commercial secrets'; builds on prior Reuters reporting that Tesla's self-published FSD stats were 'highly exaggerated'

Additional Terafab detail emerges: 10-phase project, >100M sq ft full footprint, targeted >1TW AI compute capacity annually split ~25% Optimus / 75% SpaceX; SpaceX paid Grimes County, TX $10M to satisfy a tax-abatement deadline; county commissioners told the project is a 'done deal'

Michael Burry (Scion Asset Management) covers his TSLA short (opened Jun 30 at $416.22); same reporting batch shows him adding to Micron shorts and rolling into a larger QQQ put position — a broad risk-rotation, not a TSLA-specific thesis reversal

Secondary-sourced reports (TipRanks, CoinCentral) of a Nevada Transportation Authority robotaxi-related filing/approval contributing to Thursday's rally; exact scope unconfirmed — could be the pending 5,000-vehicle commercial AVNC permit (Docket 26-05015) or a narrower procedural filing; primary docket unverified

Tesla ends its ~1,021-day Swedish IF Metall strike by buying out every remaining striking union member rather than signing a collective agreement; union calls it unprecedented in the Swedish labor market; industrial action formally ends Aug 19

Nevada Transportation Authority interim order confirms Tesla Robotaxi LLC's AVNC Permit (Docket 26-05015): capped at just 10 fully autonomous vehicles, geofenced to the Las Vegas Strip corridor, roads ≤45mph only — a fraction of the 5,000-vehicle request that drove Thursday's rally on unconfirmed reports; any fleet/area expansion requires separate NTA approval

Austin permit filings show Tesla leased a facility on St. Elmo Road, planning 80 wireless chargers for the Cybercab fleet — first physical-infrastructure evidence behind the 'launch as soon as this month' reporting
Tesla launches a Certified Pre-Owned (CPO) vehicle program in the US and Puerto Rico: 115-point inspection, 1-year/10,000-mile warranty; no disclosed volume or revenue target
The Information: Tesla preps public Cybercab (no-wheel/no-pedal) launch in Austin 'as soon as this month' — starts with employee rides on public roads before rolling into paid robotaxi service
Roadster/SpaceX-thruster reveal detail: routine scaled back to a driverless liftoff-only demo using cold-gas thrusters at McGregor, TX, spectators kept at safety distance; still no confirmed date

FSD v14.3.6 regression: vehicle attempts an already-passed highway exit at 68mph on Quebec's Autoroute 55, driver intervenes; feeds standing NHTSA degraded-visibility/detection probe (EA26002) narrative

Driverless Robotaxi in Austin rams through traffic bollards after hesitating instead of reversing; video surfaces on r/SelfDrivingCars, contradicts VP of AI Ashok Elluswamy's Q2 earnings-call claim of 'zero notable incidents' across 380k+ unsupervised robotaxi miles

Nevada Transportation Authority unanimously approves permits for Tesla (up to 5,000 vehicles), Uber (1,000, via Motional/Zoox), and Waymo (1,000) to run commercial robotaxi service across all of Clark County — reversing the Jul 27/Aug 14 order that had capped Tesla at 10 vehicles geofenced to the Strip; Tesla's Cybercab lead Eric Early calls 5,000 'always... a ceiling,' says the company would be satisfied reaching ~2,500 within a year; local taxi/livery operators opposed the permits as moving too fast

Tesla recalls ~5.7M combined vehicles in China (2.96M for emergency door-handle visibility/accessibility post-collision — remedied via warning labels plus an OTA update that auto-lowers windows after a crash; 2.74M for driver-monitoring — adds cabin-camera eye-tracking to the assisted-driving system) as part of an 11-automaker, ~4M+ vehicle industry-wide regulatory crackdown; China will also ban concealed door handles from 2027, a design Tesla popularized — no physical part replacement required, but sets a design-standard precedent

Tesla confirms it will reveal European Semi launch details (local pricing, Megacharger rollout plans, delivery timeline) at IAA Transportation Hannover, Sept 15-20 2026 (press day Sept 14) — first concrete step toward commercializing the Semi in Europe; no range, pricing, or on-sale date disclosed yet

Trade press (Electrek, TeslaNorth, Benzinga et al.) reports Tesla has quietly discontinued its Solar Roof tile product (~10 years after launch), telling certified installers the tiles are no longer orderable and pulling the product from its website; company shifts Energy focus entirely to traditional solar panels (incl. new 420W panels from Giga New York); no official Tesla statement, cited as not financially viable. Solar Roof volumes have been immaterial for years — Energy segment revenue is overwhelmingly Megapack/Powerwall — so direct P&L impact is negligible, but it reinforces a narrative of Tesla product bets not scaling

Chinese social-media rumor claims Tesla emptied its Shanghai FSD/data-center team (read as a setback to China FSD monetization); Tesla/Tesla China deny same-day to local press (data center 'operating normally,' hiring accelerating); stock dips ~1% intraday before mostly recovering

Dashcam video shows Tesla FSD approaching a railroad crossing at 9mph with flashing signals and an audible train; driver manually brakes to avoid the tracks (Electrek); feeds NHTSA's standing degraded-visibility engineering analysis (EA26002, ~3.2M vehicles)

Musk announces SpaceX will manufacture its own gas-turbine parts in-house to bring natural-gas power online up to 18 months faster for AI data centers, alongside solar; framed as reinforcing the shared Tesla-SpaceX AI-infrastructure narrative (Tesla Energy solar/storage read-through, Terafab); TSLA closes +5.51% at $367.95 Monday on ~46% above-average volume

Electrek investigative-series update documents a 4th fatal crash (Batavia, IL, Mar 2026, passenger death) where Tesla's own NHTSA filing lists driver-assist as 'Verified Engaged' during the fatal turn, tying it to the same pattern as the standing Clute TX/Lake Mary FL/Mesa AZ cases and the open EA26002 probe
August European registration data mixed by country: France +279% YoY, Denmark +104% YoY vs. Norway -79%, Sweden -41%; UK/Germany data still pending

Tesla settles the Mendoza v. Tesla fatal Autopilot 'fire truck' wrongful-death lawsuit (N.D. Cal.) before trial, avoiding jury scrutiny of 'Autopilot' marketing claims a judge had called 'plausibly misleading'
Tesla China August wholesale sales: 86,166 units, +3.57% YoY but -7.92% MoM, snapping the streak of sequential monthly gains

Tesla holds invite-only Cybercab Austin launch event confirming the two-seat, no-steering-wheel/no-pedal robotaxi runs on AI4 compute, emphasizing fleet economics for commercial operators over consumer specs, with no final MSRP, order button, or delivery date disclosed; same day, Tesla opens a web form soliciting third parties interested in buying/operating Cybercab fleets or mobility hubs — a shift from an all in-house robotaxi model; stock reaction muted despite a ~6% pre-event intraday rally

CNN/AP piece syndicated widely on Cybercab-launch day frames Tesla as trailing Waymo (~380K cumulative unsupervised robotaxi miles vs Waymo's ~500K weekly paid rides) and flags Rivian's planned 50K R2 robotaxis for Uber plus Lucid/Nuro/Wayve supply deals

NHTSA opens a formal investigation into the process and technical data Tesla used to certify the two-seat, no-steering-wheel/no-pedal Cybercab as exempt from federal motor-vehicle safety standards, hours after Wednesday's Austin public launch

Friday's Cybercab certification concern escalates into a formally named NHTSA Audit Query, explicitly compared to the multi-year Zoox precedent; same-day RBC/Wells Fargo notes flag unanswered pricing/production questions and reported early Austin rider complaints; TSLA closes -5.92% at $354.08 on 1.7x ADV20

Musk confirms via X (Sunday Sep 6) that Tesla is testing Robotaxi in Austin with zero occupants — no rider, no safety driver — after an X user posted video of the empty vehicle driving itself; first fully-driverless public-road demonstration reported, layered on top of NHTSA's Sep 4 Audit Query into Cybercab's no-steering-wheel FMVSS certification

Slovenia's traffic safety authority clears Tesla FSD (Supervised), the 6th European market to approve it (after Netherlands, Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, Belgium); Uber shares fall ~4% same-day on Cybercab/robotaxi competitive-threat framing while TSLA rallies ~4% to $368.16 despite a 600pt Dow selloff

NBC News (Sep 9, citing Sep 8 remarks): Austin Fire Dept Capt. Matthew McElearney says Tesla trained first responders to move a stalled/disabled Cybercab via its touchscreen (no steering wheel/pedals) but calls it 'not the silver bullet' and wants federal standards; Tesla's own emergency-responder safety plan says a stalled Cybercab may need to be 'pushed' — a concrete new fact layered onto the open NHTSA Cybercab Audit Query (AQ26002, opened Sep 3-4)

Morgan Stanley (Andrew Percoco) lifts its Tesla Semi/autonomous-trucking bull-case scenario to $840 (from $820) on a new per-mile autonomous-driving software-revenue model ($12k-18k/month, ~$0.85-$1/mile per truck; ~$17B software revenue and $7.5B incremental EBIT by 2040 if Tesla reaches 82,000 Semis); Hold rating and $400 base-case PT unchanged; record diesel prices (~$6+) cited as an added tailwind

Tesla confirms next-gen Roadster unveil for Oct 1 2026 (X post + website countdown), teaser shows SpaceX-thruster imagery, Musk calls it 'out of this world'; Musk has already flagged production is still 12-18 months out post-reveal

Goldman Sachs (Mark Delaney) cuts Q3 2026 delivery estimate to 435,000 vehicles from 490,000 (~11% cut), citing weaker-than-expected demand across US, China, and Europe offsetting export strength; now below Visible Alpha consensus (456,000) and Kalshi prediction-market centering (~480,000); Neutral rating and $360 PT unchanged

NHTSA issues a formal Special Order (Sep 10, signed by Chief Counsel Peter Simshauser) escalating the Cybercab certification Audit Query (AQ26002): demands a sworn-oath affidavit from a responsible Tesla officer answering 21 detailed requests on how the no-steering-wheel/no-pedal Cybercab was self-certified to FMVSS, due Sep 30; discloses exposure up to $139.35M in civil penalties plus potential criminal liability for false certification -- a materially harder escalation than the 'audit query opened' framing previously in state

Tesla dispatches its robotics team to Ningbo, China to conduct a formal Optimus mass-production supply-chain audit (team arrived Sep 16, audit began Sep 17), reviewing quality-consistency standards and transferring US manufacturing know-how to Chinese component suppliers (actuators: Ningbo Tuopu; sensors: Ningbo Joyson; thermal: Zhejiang Sanhua); read as confirmation Tesla remains on track toward its ~50,000-unit 2026 Optimus target

Goldman Sachs further cuts its Q4 2026 Tesla delivery forecast to 475,000 from 515,000 (Sep 19), on top of its already-known Q3 cut to 435,000 (Sep 17), framing weekly US/China/Europe tracking data as pointing to 'structural' rather than temporary demand weakness; cites August US deliveries of ~40,816 units, -26% YoY, with demand flat since the September 2025 EV tax-credit expiry

Barclays (Dan Levy) raises its Tesla Q3 2026 delivery view to 475,000 units, above ~466,000 Street/Bloomberg consensus and well above Goldman's 435,000 bear case, citing FSD progress; maintains Equal Weight, $370 PT, calls auto fundamentals 'an afterthought' to the AI story; stock nonetheless edged lower intraday Friday on the news

California Civil Rights Dept. v. Tesla race-discrimination trial opens in Oakland Superior Court (Judge Peter Borkon), scheduled to run through Oct 30 2026; a prior individual case on the same Fremont-plant fact pattern produced a $137M jury verdict (later reduced)

Reports name specific Optimus Gen-3 supplier-audit targets in China (Tuopu Group, Sanhua Intelligent Controls, Joyson Electronics -- actuators/structural/thermal parts) across Ningbo/Hangzhou/Shanghai, tied to the ~50,000-unit 2026 Optimus target
Tesla in-house attorney accused of misleading a witness ahead of the Oakland race-discrimination bench trial; CRD seeks a protective order
Fitch assigns Tesla its first-ever investment-grade credit rating (BBB), lowering its cost of capital and signaling reduced balance-sheet risk to bond and equity investors

Tesla Semi wins a 2,500-truck 'ZET SCALE' fleet order (founding shippers Microsoft and PepsiCo), roughly doubling the US electric heavy-truck fleet, two days ahead of the Nevada Semi factory inauguration
Czech Republic recognizes Tesla FSD (Supervised), the 7th EU country to approve it, following the Dutch RDW provisional approval
